arxiv-2303-07702.title: Carbon-Neutralized Joint User Association and Base Station Switching for Green Cellular Networks
arxiv-2303-07702.creator: Chien-Sheng Yang, Carlson Lin and I-Kang Fu
arxiv-2303-07702.description: Abstract Mitigating climate change and its impacts is one of the sustainable development goals (SDGs) required by United Nations for an urgent action. Increasing carbon emissions due to human activities is the root cause to climate change. Telecommunication networks that provide service connectivity to mobile users contribute great amount of carbon emissions by consuming lots of non-renewable energy sources.

arxiv-2403-08829.title: Mitigating Biases in Collective Decision-Making: Enhancing Performance in the Face of Fake News
arxiv-2403-08829.creator: Axel Abels, Elias Fernandez Domingos, Ann Nowé, Tom Lenaerts
arxiv-2403-08829.description: Abstract Individual and social biases undermine the effectiveness of human advisers by inducing judgment errors which can disadvantage protected groups. In this paper, we study the influence these biases can have in the pervasive problem of fake news by evaluating human participants’ capacity to identify false headlines.

arxiv-2408-03636.title: Time is Not Enough: Time-Frequency based Explanation for Time-Series Black-Box Models
arxiv-2408-03636.creator: Hyunseung Chung, Sumin Jo, Yeonsu Kwon, Edward Choi
arxiv-2408-03636.description: Abstract . Despite the massive attention given to time-series explanations due to their extensive applications, a notable limitation in existing approaches is their primary reliance on the time-domain. This overlooks the inherent characteristic of time-series data containing both time and frequency features.

arxiv-2505-13228.title: Sensitivity to New Physics Phenomena in Anomaly Detection: A Study of Untunable Hyperparameters
arxiv-2505-13228.creator: Fernando Abreu de Souza, Maura Barros, Nuno F. Castro, Miguel Crispim Romão, Céu Neiva, Rute Pedro
arxiv-2505-13228.description: Abstract The search for physics beyond the Standard Model (BSM) at collider experiments requires model-independent strategies to avoid missing possible discoveries of unexpected signals. Anomaly detection (AD) techniques offer a promising approach by identifying deviations from the Standard Model (SM) and have been extensively studied. The sensitivity of these methods to untunable hyperparameters has not been systematically compared, however.

arxiv-2506-11319.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Adel Chehade, Edoardo Ragusa Paolo Gastaldo, and Rodolfo Zunino. This paper presents a hardware-efficient deep neural network (DNN), optimized through hardware-aware neural architecture search (HW-NAS); the DNN supports the classification of session-level encrypted traffic on resource-constrained Internet of Things (IoT) and edge devices. Thanks to HW-NAS, a 1D convolutional neural network (CNN) is tailored on the ISCX VPN-nonVPN dataset to meet strict memory and computational limits while achieving robust performance.

arxiv-2511-14532.creator: Subhajit Ghosh, Kimberly K. Boddy, Tien-Tien Yu
arxiv-2511-14532.description: Abstract We study the cosmological impact of ultralight dark matter (ULDM) with a quadratic coupling to Standard Model particles. In addition to the suppression of small-scale power from ULDM itself, the coupling induces a variation of fundamental constants that is modulated by the ULDM oscillatory field value.

pmc-10657262.title: The Effect of Combined Intervention on Improvement of Early Lexical Development in Minimally Verbal Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
pmc-10657262.creator: Salman Abdi, Maryam Tarameshlu, Noureddin Nakhostin Ansari, Leila Ghelichi, Mitra Hakim Shooshtari
pmc-10657262.description: BackgroundAutism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder defined by severe communication deficits and limited and repetitive behavioral tendencies. There are several treatment approaches and methods for minimally verbal children with ASD; nonetheless, there is inconclusive evidence about how early lexical development could be improved.

pmc-10753427.title: Pharmaceutical Agents as Potential Drivers in the Development of Early-Onset Colorectal Cancer: Case-Control Study
pmc-10753427.creator: Irit Ben-Aharon, Ran Rotem, Cheli Melzer-Cohen, Gilad Twig, Andrea Cercek, Elizabeth Half, Tal Goshen-Lago, Gabriel Chodik, David Kelsen, Amaryllis Mavragani, Travis Sanchez, TsungChun Lee, Shinichi Matsuda, Ketan Gupta
pmc-10753427.description: BackgroundThe incidence of early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC) rose abruptly in the mid 1990s, is continuing to increase, and has now been noted in many countries. By 2030, 25% of American patients diagnosed with rectal cancer will be 49 years or younger.

pmc-11528668.title: Deciphering the CNS-glioma dialogue: Advanced insights into CNS-glioma communication pathways and their therapeutic potential
pmc-11528668.creator: Lu Zhang, Yajing Wang, Xiaoxi Cai, Xinyuan Mao, Haitao Sun
pmc-11528668.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The field of cancer neuroscience has rapidly evolved, shedding light on the complex interplay between the nervous system and cancer, with a particular focus on the relationship between the central nervous system (CNS) and gliomas. Recent advancements have underscored the critical influence of CNS activity on glioma progression, emphasizing the roles of neurons and neuroglial cells in both the onset and evolution of gliomas.

pmc-11904172.title: Van Wyk-Grumbach syndrome and its clinical heterogeneity: A case report
pmc-11904172.creator: Krisha Jain, Shreya Siera Honarius, Reema Reji, Ravi Sangoi, Saurabh Mutha, Mayur Wanjari
pmc-11904172.description: This case report presents a 6-year-old female with Van Wyk-Grumbach syndrome, highlighting its astounding clinical presentations and the challenges in its diagnosis and management. Although the disease is rare, Van Wyk-Grumbach Syndrome can have a devastating and serious impact in young boys and girls by affecting their hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis.
